title: Distractor_software: Automated maze-task distractor generation for English, German, and Arabic
description:
Distractor_software generates maze-task distractor stimuli for psycholinguistic experiments in English, German, and Arabic. For every word of a sentence it selects a real word of similar length and frequency that a Transformer language model (GPT-2) finds highly implausible in context.

Candidates are filtered by part of speech using lexicons built from published lexical norms (SUBTLEX-US, dlexDB, CAMeL Tools), optionally by semantic dissimilarity (fastText), and every run writes a per-position quality report.

The tool was developed to produce the stimuli for the Master's thesis Dissecting the Maze Task with Eye-Tracking (University of Stuttgart) and adapts the original Maze repository by Victoria Boyce.

Licensing: the code is MIT. The bundled part-of-speech lexicons are not covered by the MIT licence; each follows its source's terms (English, SUBTLEX-US: non-commercial research use; German, dlexDB: CC BY-SA 4.0; Arabic, CAMeL Tools data: GPL-2.0). See src/maze_automate/lexicons/LICENSE.md.
